evals.prompt: 幫我在 app 裡加一個書籤功能，用戶可以收藏文章，回頭能找到。
evals.expected_output: 觸發 Lane A 用法 A。輸出改寫後的驗證劇本：造數據（≥3 篇文章）、收藏/取消/列表恢復的正路徑斷言、≥2 邊界（重複收藏同一篇、中文標題、空列表）、失敗協議（修到全部通過）、環境工具（Web→CDP / 桌面→啟動+截圖）。不改需求本身，只補驗證權。
expectations: 輸出包含造數據步驟且數量明確
正路徑斷言查具體結果（如列表只出現已收藏項），不是『無報錯』
至少 2 個邊界（重複收藏 / 空 / 中文至少佔 2）
含失敗協議：任何一步失敗繼續修直到全部通過
含環境工具對齊（CDP 或啟動+截圖等，不是『人工檢查』）

evals.prompt: 我的項目裡 agent 總是找不到功能入口，每次都要我自己截圖給它看頁面在哪。好煩。
evals.expected_output: 診斷為 L0→L2 缺口（feature map 缺失），推薦建 feature map 卡。輸出用 templates/feature-map-template.md 結構的示例卡，強調驗證步驟是卡的承重部分 + 地圖時效錨（驗證失敗先懷疑地圖過期）。
expectations: 診斷為 feature map / L2 缺口，不是『prompt 寫好點』
輸出 feature map 卡結構示例（入口/驗證步驟/相關代碼/常見問題）
含地圖腐爛防禦（時效錨 / 驗證失敗先查地圖）
不建議繼續人工截圖餵圖（那是 L0 循環）

evals.prompt: I keep telling the agent 'don't import across feature directories'. Must have said it 5 times this week. It keeps forgetting.
evals.expected_output: 觸發 L3 硬約束路徑：違反頻率×後果判準（5 次 → 候選）。推薦 lint no-restricted-imports / import 邊界掃描 + CI 掛。給出升級流程關鍵步驟：warn 先行收集誤報 → 誤報裁決 → 轉 fail；報錯 message 寫成對 agent 的現場教學。明確說『不要再靠模型記住』。
expectations: 推薦 lint/import 邊界掃描 + CI，而非把這句話寫進 AGENTS.md
含 warn 先行 → 誤報裁決 → 轉 fail 的升級流程
報錯 message 面向 agent（含原因與改法）
指出 soft 層（AGENTS.md）是錯誤載體

evals.prompt: 我的驗證腳本全綠，agent 說功能沒問題，但用戶回報搜索中文出亂碼。驗證不是都過了嗎？
evals.expected_output: 診斷為假綠（斷言弱：只查無報錯/exit code，未查結果；或測試數據不含中文）。兩個動作：修斷言（查結果+中文邊界）+ 護欄反測（拿已知壞例子反向測斷言——故意引入亂碼 bug，斷言必須紅）。若 agent 自驗證可信度被質疑，提及驗證者不得是生成者。
expectations: 診斷為斷言弱/數據缺失的假綠，不是『agent 又錯了』
提出用已知壞例子反向測斷言（護欄反測）
建議把中文邊界寫進驗證規格
可提及驗證者不得是生成者（role-pipeline）

evals.prompt: 驗證基建跑得不錯，我想讓 agent 直接自動合併 PR 到 main，跟上潮流。現在就開嗎？
evals.expected_output: 觸發放權不等式：先過 templates/autonomy-checklist.md 前置清單。若清單未過（L2 地圖/L3 紅線/L4 eval 近 3 次全綠任一缺）→ 停在本級給最小補齊清單。強調監控指標是 revert rate + 事後 bug 率，不是吞吐量；含自動收權觸發器。明確反對『跟上潮流』作為放權理由。
expectations: 不放權於清單未過之前——引用放權不等式
要求 revert rate + 事後 bug 率作為監控指標，明確排除吞吐量指標
含自動收權路徑/觸發器
建議漸進：單任務自驗證 → 單域 → 擴域，不一步到位全 main

evals.prompt: 就寫個一次性腳本把 CSV 轉個格式，也要搞你那套驗證劇本嗎？
evals.expected_output: 觸發降級出口：明說 L1 即終點甚至更輕——一次性腳本、可隨手回滾的改動不值得 L2+。直接給一句含最小驗證的 prompt（跑一次+抽查輸出+exit code），不鋪基建。明確說不鋪。
expectations: 明說不需要完整劇本/基建（降級出口）
仍給最小驗證（自己跑 + 抽查輸出 + exit code）
不推薦建 feature map / verification.md / CI 紅線

evals.prompt: AGENTS.md 和你這套 verification / feature map 有什麼區別？我是不是寫好 AGENTS.md 就夠了？
evals.expected_output: 說清分工：AGENTS.md 是 soft 約束（靠模型記住，會忘），四件套是機制（feature map=知道在哪、verification=能自證、硬約束=機制擋、eval=監控基建本身）。判準：會被忘的約束升 hard；掃代碼掃得出的不寫進文件。引用『說過三次』判準。
expectations: 區分 soft（記憶）與 hard（機制）兩層
指出 AGENTS.md 會被遺忘，報錯/紅線不會
不否定 AGENTS.md 的存在價值，但給出內容遷移判準（說過三次→升級）
可指向 repo-docs-sop 作為文件規劃補充

evals.prompt: Our AI agent wrote a user-profile CRUD endpoint. Standard POST/GET/PATCH, Postgres, nothing fancy. Team wants me to 'just ship it, tests are green'. Should I run the full discipline here or just let it through?
evals.expected_output: Grade L1 or low-L2. Open minimal gates (smoke + human skim critical path). Do NOT open mutation testing / full metrics — that is over-gating an exploration/routine task. Still runs reverse-gate screen (all pass) and spec self-check.
expectations: Assigns a low grade (L1 or low L2) appropriate to routine reversible CRUD
Does NOT open full mutation testing or full metric gates for this grade
Still runs the reverse-gate screens before opening any gate
Does not STOP (the task is gate-catchable and reversible)

evals.prompt: It's just a small change to our billing endpoint — adding a discount_code field to the charge request. But the endpoint already handles idempotency keys and retries from the payment gateway. AI says it's a one-liner, tests pass, ship it.
evals.expected_output: Detects the L3 corner (touches payment/irreversible path with existing idempotency/retry protocol). Runs the WHOLE task at L3 per cross-bucket rule — does NOT average down to L2 just because the diff is one line. Delegates spec gate to protocol-adversarial-design due to idempotency/retry character. Requires L3 human line-read of the core path.
expectations: Identifies the L3 corner (payment + idempotency + retry = irreversible / protocol character)
Does NOT grade down to L2 because the diff is small (no averaging the cross-bucket corner down)
Runs the entire task at L3 including human line-read of core paths
Delegates the spec gate to protocol-adversarial-design due to idempotency/retry
Rejects 'ship it, tests green' as sufficient for this grade

evals.prompt: I'm not even sure this module is modeled at the right abstraction level. The AI's code passes all tests and metrics look clean, but something feels off about whether we split this into a service or kept it inline. Can you verify the quality?
evals.expected_output: STOP at reverse-gate Screen 1 — the quality hinges on abstract-level choice, which gates cannot catch. Category disclosure applies. Falls back to human reading. Does NOT pretend gates can judge the abstraction.
expectations: Outputs STOP at the reverse gate (Screen 1: defect class not gate-catchable)
Names abstract-level choice / architecture smell as structurally uncatchable by gating
Recommends human reading, does not run the verify/metric gates
Does NOT claim 'metrics clean + tests pass = quality verified'

evals.prompt: The AI agent that generated the code also ran the tests and reported 100% coverage, complexity 3, all passing. It says we're good to ship. This is an L2 internal admin feature.
evals.expected_output: Flags the self-declared gate pass (anti-pattern 6) — the verifier was the generator. Requires re-running verify/metric gates from a distinct agent or refutation-instructed stage. Does NOT accept the AI's self-reported gate results.
expectations: Identifies that the generator also ran the verify (self-grading anti-pattern)
Does NOT accept self-reported coverage/complexity/passed as the gate result
Requires the verifier to be a distinct agent or refutation-instructed stage
References role-pipeline / anti-pattern 6

evals.prompt: Ran the verify gate at L2. Mutation testing killed 9 of 10 mutants on a routine feature — that's way more edge cases than an L2 should surface. But the grade's already set, so let's just keep the L2 result and move on.
evals.expected_output: Triggers feedback-upgrade: mutation failure density far above the grade's prediction falsifies the L2 grade. Re-grades (up, toward L3) and re-runs denser gates. Does NOT keep the L2 result just because the grade was fixed at step 0.
expectations: Triggers feedback-upgrade based on high mutation failure density vs grade prediction
Re-grades upward (toward L3) rather than holding L2
Does NOT keep the prior L2 gate result as 'already passed'
States that downstream evidence reopens the step-0 grade

evals.prompt: AI refactored a 200-line function into ten 20-line functions. Cyclomatic complexity dropped from 12 to 4. Coverage still 100%. Looks much cleaner now — can we pass the metric gate?
evals.expected_output: Does NOT pass on the single complexity metric. Requires mutation-score cross-check: if complexity dropped but mutation score also dropped, the split was cosmetic, not real simplification. Combines metrics, does not pass on complexity alone.
expectations: Does NOT pass the gate on cyclomatic complexity alone
Requires the mutation-score cross-check for the refactor
Flags the split-to-game pattern (ten trivial functions vs one coherent one)
Reads metrics in combination, not per-metric pass lines

evals.prompt: Write me the acceptance criteria for our new onboarding flow — make it feel welcoming and natural for first-time users.
evals.expected_output: STOP at reverse-gate Screen 2 — spec is irreducibly fuzzy ('feel welcoming/natural') with non-trivial effort. Reading code / ordinary UX acceptance is cheaper than a cage that won't hold. Does NOT force hard invariants on a tone/feel task.
expectations: Outputs STOP at Screen 2 (spec not hardenable at reasonable cost)
Does NOT manufacture hard invariants for a 'feel/tone' requirement
Suggests ordinary UX acceptance / human reading as the cheaper alternative
Does not delegate to protocol-adversarial-design (no protocol character)

evals.prompt: I need to understand what this legacy auth middleware does before we touch it. Can you run the quality gates on it to tell me if it's any good?
evals.expected_output: STOP at reverse-gate Screen 3 — the task is comprehending existing code, not generating new code. Gates do not produce comprehension. Recommends reading the code instead. Does NOT run the generate→verify pipeline on existing code.
expectations: Outputs STOP at Screen 3 (task is comprehension, not generation)
Does NOT run the generation/verify/metric pipeline on existing code
Recommends reading the code as the correct action
Recognizes gates do not produce comprehension

evals.prompt: We shipped the AI-generated feature two weeks ago and it's causing intermittent data loss in production. Where did the discipline fail — and what do we fix?
evals.expected_output: Runs the self-loop: locates which gate leaked (spec weak? verify didn't cover? metric gamed? grade mis-called? self-grading?) rather than re-running the whole pipeline. Fixes only that gate's output. Post-incident diagnostic, not a pre-ship run.
expectations: Treats this as a self-loop diagnostic, not a fresh pipeline run
Locates the specific leaking gate rather than re-running everything
Considers grade mis-call / self-grading / spec-weakness / metric-gaming as candidate leaks
Does NOT respond by re-grading and re-running all gates from scratch

evals.prompt: This is an irreversible data migration — once it runs we can't roll back, and a bug corrupts production data permanently. The AI agent can generate it fast. Let's just do L2 gates since it's a one-time script.
evals.expected_output: Grades L3 (irreversible + high failure cost). Does NOT allow L2 gates on an irreversible task. Reverse-gate Screen 4 would STOP if only sampled gates were proposed — upgrades to L3 with full mutation + human line-read. Single-use does not lower the grade.
expectations: Grades L3 due to irreversibility + permanent data corruption risk
Does NOT downgrade to L2 because it is a one-time script
Requires full mutation testing + line-level human read for this grade
Screen 4 logic applies: irreversible harm + only sampled gates = STOP or upgrade
